A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EBC/QD-IRL research. All 20 pages, including Appendices A–L, are present and readable through text extraction and rendering, supporting comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original robot-locomotion simulation results, including benchmark comparisons, sensitivity analyses, demonstration studies, and adaptation experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original simulation results in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–3 retain the same episode-based EBC bonus, PPGA procedure, and GAIL, VAIL, and DiffAIL implementations. The broader title introduces no procedural change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Halfcheetah, Walker2d, Humanoid, Hopper, and Ant, with the same behavior measures and hurdles, motor-failure, and friction adaptation scenarios. The broader policy-learning framing adds no evaluated domain or task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the experiments. Table 8 retains GAIL, VAIL, DiffAIL, GIRIL, AIRL, Max-Ent IRL, and PPGA with true reward alongside the EBC variants; the other comparisons also retain their respective methods.

E3.justification: Both retain the four-demonstration main benchmark, training budgets, QD metrics, CCDF evaluation, and adaptation without retraining. Experimental settings in Section 4 and Appendices C–J are unchanged.

E4.justification: The q sensitivity study, archive visualizations, demonstration quantity/diversity/quality study, and perturbation-based adaptation analyses are identical. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both report three-seed means and standard deviations for benchmark experiments, Tukey HSD tests in Appendix H, and adaptation IQM values with 95% confidence intervals in Figure 5. Run information and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported numerical values, plotted results, and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 8 reports Humanoid QD-Scores of 5.31 × 10^6 for GAIL-EBC and 1.86 × 10^6 for GAIL in both versions.

T1.justification: Lemma 3.1, its assumptions and proof, the EBC derivation, and the mathematical background in Appendix A are unchanged. No definition, theorem, or mathematical reasoning is revised.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, final contribution bullet, and conclusion broaden the stated contribution from diverse robot locomotion to learning behaviorally diverse policies generally. This is limited reframing: v2 already claimed potential applicability to any IRL application requiring diverse policies, and the performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and mechanism explanations are retained. Appendices K–L preserve the limitations concerning imitation-reward archive updates and applicability beyond MDPs or policy-gradient optimization, together with the same future-work discussion.

D1.justification: Both provide the same code link, implementation libraries, hardware and training-time disclosures, demonstration details, and hyperparameter tables in Appendices C–E. No reproducibility information is added or revised.

R1.justification: The references and discussion of prior research are unchanged, including the distinction between EBC's episode-level bonus and Yu et al.'s single-step exploration bonus. The broader application framing does not revise these relationships or novelty claims.

P1.justification: The title and running headers replace 'Robot Locomotion' with 'Policy'. A few abstract, introduction, and conclusion sentences adopt broader policy-diversity wording; section order, appendix organization, and the remaining prose are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–9, Tables 1–11, and algorithm blocks retain identical content, formatting, and placement. Page organization is unchanged; the limited title and prose edits introduce only local text reflow.

improvement.justification: v4 broadens the headline framing to policy diversity, consistent with applicability already discussed in v2. The methods, evidence, reproducibility information, explanations, and limitations remain unchanged, leaving no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
